answer: For each submission, the protocol draws unpredictable reviewers to run hidden canary checks. A canary plants plausible junk in the work; reviewers who approve it, or identities that coordinate their verdicts, lose stake and credentials. A Sybil operator must keep accounts separate and pay for honest review, while each caught cluster forfeits its stake and waits to rebuild. A vine of linked accounts may wander into the same canyon of checks, exposing its shared operator.
